requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g) || []; const bad = []; const s = text; for (const x of m) { const c = x.replace(/^"category"\s*:\s*"/, '').replace(/"$/, ''); if (!/^[A-Za-z ]+ – [a-z ]+$/.test(c) && !/^Floor – all brands$/.test(c)) bad.push({start: s.indexOf(x), end: s.indexOf(x)+x.length, why: 'category not in taxonomy form: ' + c}); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' malformed category name(s)' : 'category names well-formed', spans: bad }; }
means: Each category value is checked for the 'Family – qualifier' form with an en dash; membership in the 39-item list cannot be checked without the taxonomy text, so only form is checked.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; const dur = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const D = dur ? (+dur[1])*60+(+dur[2]) : null; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]), e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (D!==null && e>D) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span runs past duration'}); if (e<=s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span end not after start'}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' bad span(s)' : 'spans valid', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span is read as mm:ss start–end; checks it ends within the clip's duration and that end is after start.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (!/^(Low|Medium|High)$/.test(m[1]) && m[1] !== 'Floor') bad.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'risk not Low, Medium or High' }); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' bad risk value(s)' : 'risk levels valid', spans: bad }; }
means: Each risk value in the label is Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasFire = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(hasFire && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no firearm and floor label together' : 'firearms label and Floor – all brands both present', spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands'), end: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands') + 18, why: 'Floor label beside a firearms label' }] }; }
means: The label does not carry both a firearms category and Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text, request, material) => { const hasFloor = /"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); const cats = (text.match(/"category"\s*:/g)||[]).length; const floorOnly = hasFloor && cats===1 && /"risk"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text) && !/"span"/.test(text); const noFlag = cats===0; const ok = !(noFlag) || floorOnly; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no-flag rule holds' : 'clip with no flagged category not labelled Floor with no timecode', spans: ok ? [] : [{start:0,end:text.length,why:'no flagged category requires Floor risk and no span'}] }; }
means: If the label has no categories, checks it is the Floor label with risk Floor and no span; otherwise passes.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad = []; const re = /"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"[\s\S]*?"evidence"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (!m[2].trim()) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'empty evidence for ' + m[1]}); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' category(ies) without evidence' : 'all categories carry evidence', spans: bad }; }
means: Each category has a non-empty evidence string; whether the words are copied from the transcript is checked under step 17.

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text, request, material) => { const order = {Floor:0,Low:1,Medium:2,High:3}; const ov = text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/); const risks = [...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); if (!ov) return {ok:false,detail:'no overall',spans:[]}; const max = risks.reduce((a,r)=> (order[r]??-1)>(order[a]??-1)?r:a, risks[0]||'Floor'); const ok = max===ov[1]; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'overall is the highest risk' : 'overall '+ov[1]+' differs from highest '+max, spans: ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'overall mismatch'}] }; }
means: Checks the overall value equals the highest risk among the categories.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; const dur=text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const D=dur?(+dur[1])*60+(+dur[2]):null; while((m=re.exec(text))){const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]),e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if(e<=s||(D!==null&&e>D)) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start or past duration'});} return {ok:bad.length===0,detail:bad.length?bad.length+' bad span(s)':'span order and bounds hold',spans:bad}; }
means: Checks each span's end is after its start and within the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(/frame/i.test(m[1])||/\d+\s*f\b/.test(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'frame count in span'}); } return {ok:bad.length===0,detail:bad.length?'frame count found in span':'no frame counts in spans',spans:bad}; }
means: Checks no span contains a frame count or frame unit.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.

source: (text, request, material) => {
const bad = [];
const norm = s => String(s || '').toLowerCase().replace(/[\u2018\u2019\u201C\u201D]/g, '"').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const tr = norm((material || []).filter(m => /transcript/i.test(m.name || '')).map(m => m.text).join(' '));
let m;
while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
let raw = m[1];
try { raw = JSON.parse('"' + raw + '"'); } catch (e) {}
const ev = norm(raw);
const empty = /^(the )?transcript is empty$|^nothing in the transcript is flagged$/.test(ev);
if (ev && tr && !empty && !tr.includes(ev))
bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'evidence not found verbatim in transcript'});
return {
ok: bad.length === 0,
detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' evidence string(s) not verbatim in transcript' : 'evidence is verbatim from transcript',
spans: bad
means: Each evidence string appears verbatim in the transcript material.

requirements.statement: A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text, request, material) => { const names=[...text.matchAll(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); const seen=new Set(); const dup=[]; for(const n of names){ if(seen.has(n)) dup.push({start:0,end:text.length,why:'category listed twice: '+n}); seen.add(n);} return {ok:dup.length===0,detail:dup.length?dup.length+' repeated category':'no repeated category',spans:dup}; }
means: Checks no category name appears more than once in the label.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch(e) { return {ok:false,detail:'label is not valid JSON',spans:[]}; } const keys=Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys==='categories,clip,duration,overall'; return {ok,detail:ok?'label has exactly the four keys':'keys are: '+keys,spans:ok?[]:[{start:0,end:text.length,why:'extra or missing keys'}]}; }
means: Parses the label as JSON and checks its keys are exactly clip, duration, overall, categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.

source: (text, request, material) => { const ok = true; return {ok, detail:'empty-transcript rule: checked by the transcript itself', spans:[]}; }
means: Whether the transcript is empty is a fact of the material, but the label cannot be tested for it from the label text alone; near check only, passes.

requirements.statement: My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 21 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 85.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 21 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 85 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.9 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
